https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.title_zh: 州警察：总统指示私营部门制定全面融资和实施方案
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.body_zh: 总统府已责成全国有组织私营部门为拟议中的州警察制度制定一套全面的融资与实施蓝图。总统府表示，企业必须积极参与建设维护投资、创造就业和增强经济韧性所需的安全机构。总统幕僚长兼国家警务法案总统工作组主席Femi Gbajabiamila阁下提出这一任务，并特别要求尼日利亚经济峰会组织（NESG）、商会和商业协会提出切实可行的融资方案、机构管理方案以及问责伙伴关系，以支持警务权力下放。他说，私营部门与改革成效直接相关，因为不安全状况已通过供应链中断、投资搁置、工厂扩建推迟和经济机会流失，给企业造成巨额成本。Gbajabiamila在阿布贾举行的第32届尼日利亚经济峰会“安全、稳定与经济韧性”全体会议上发言时表示，总统Bola Tinubu推动建立州警察，为企业直接参与建设支撑可持续经济增长的安全机构创造了机会。“因此，我请尼日利亚经济峰会组织把这项工作延伸到本次会议之外。认真提出私营部门关于州警察融资与实施的贡献意见，并就问责伙伴关系提出切实可行的建议。“将这项工作纳入立法进程，以及你们与州政府的沟通之中。就我们而言，我们仍负责把改革转化为公众可以信赖的保护措施。”他说。Gbajabiamila敦促商业领袖就拟议改革与州长和议员沟通，并提请他们关注有效的地方警务、创造就业与投资决策之间的关系。他解释称，企业管理机构、控制支出和评估风险的经验，可以强化新警务框架的设计与实施。他说，有组织私营部门还应提供安全失灵导致原本可行的投资无法推进的证据，使政策制定者能够确定哪里最迫切需要增加安全能力。“他的话是：“你们的参与还应提升改革的实质内容。随着立法进程推进，请审查有关融资和监督的各项建议。“请把你们管理机构和控制支出的经验带入讨论，帮助我们了解阻碍可行项目推进的安全失灵问题。”不过，这位幕僚长警告称，私营部门参与必须保持透明，绝不能损害警察机构的独立性。他说，企业可以在通信基础设施、设备维护和财务规划方面贡献专业知识，但此类伙伴关系必须在界限明确的法律和问责框架内运作。“凡是企业提供资源，这些投入都必须公布账目并接受独立审查。“公共资金必须保持稳定可靠，任何捐赠都绝不能换取对调查的影响力或优待待遇。目标是强化一项每位公民都能信赖的公共服务。”他警告道。Gbajabiamila表示，政府决心建立财政上可持续的州警察机构，并强调，希望运营自有警察服务的州必须证明其有能力承担经常性支出义务。他说，行动启动时提供车辆、制服和其他设备并不足够，还必须为人员薪资、专业培训和行动维护作出可持续安排。“财务准备同样重要。一个承担警务任务的州，必须能够在初步购置车辆和制服后继续维持该服务。“按时发放薪酬和持续培训是专业履职的必要条件。一个无法履行对警员义务的机构，会容易受到私人资助方控制以及非法公共要求的侵蚀。”他提醒道。这位幕僚长保证，对于尚未在财政或机构层面做好自建警察服务准备的州，联邦警务仍将继续运作。在介绍立法进程进展时，Gbajabiamila确认，截至2026年10月23日，已有24个州议会批准了关于设立州警察的宪法修正案，达到法定三分之二门槛。他透露，总统工作组已于10月19日向联邦司法部提交《国家警务法案》草案和29项配套修正案，供立法审议。他说，在完成审议和工作组最终审议后，这些提案将提交总统Tinubu批准，再送交国民议会。他解释称，拟议框架将使有意愿且有能力的州承担更多保护本州居民的责任，同时保留强大的联邦警察机构，以应对跨州犯罪活动和其他专业国家安全需求。Gbajabiamila说，这项改革旨在纠正一种结构性失衡，即州政府须应对不安全状况造成的后果，却无权组织警务。“让警务更贴近其服务的社区，可以改善地方情报工作，并缩短从求助到有效响应之间的时间。”他解释道。针对州警察可能被部署用于对付政治对手的担忧，他向尼日利亚人保证，拟议立法将包含可执行的保障措施、国家专业标准和独立监督机制。“警察权力可能被用于对付政治对手或弱势社区，这种担忧十分严肃。我们的应对办法是对这些权力设置可执行的限制，并在权力遭滥用时提供救济。“公民获得保护的权利不能取决于其支持谁或来自哪里。”这位幕僚长宣称。他说，该框架受益于与州政府、安全机构、公众成员以及由公共和私营部门人员组成的政策咨询委员会进行的磋商。Gbajabiamila解释企业为何应支持这项改革时表示，不安全状况对投资决策造成的影响，远远超出雇佣私人保安人员所带来的直接财务负担。他说：“现行安排的成本已经计入你们的账目。你们为额外安保和交付中断付费。“你们还承担从未作为单独费用出现的损失，例如工厂扩建推迟，或某个适宜生产的地点被排除在投资计划之外。”他论证称，如果周边社区仍不安全，企业仅靠保护自身场所无法保障持续运营。他说：“企业可以加强外围防护，但员工仍要回家，供应商仍要经过周边社区。“你们的长期安全取决于大门之外公共机构的力量。”谈及政府更广泛的安全干预措施时，Gbajabiamila表示，总统Tinubu支持通过将直升机列装陆军航空兵以及恢复100多辆经过翻新的装甲战斗车辆投入现役，推动武装部队现代化。他回忆称，总统于6月为其余3艘海军舰艇主持启用，以加强海上安全，并指出，针对原油盗取的持续行动已促进石油产量、外汇收入和政府财政收入增加。在粮食安全方面，这位幕僚长披露，政府已在19个州和联邦首都地区部署10,000名Agro-Rangers，以促进农业生产与安全保障相结合。他解释称，政府认识到，如果不保障农民能够进入自己的土地，对改良种子、农业信贷和其他支持计划的投入将难有成效。“在土地所有者因害怕而不敢耕种的农田上，改良种子和信贷获取都难以发挥作用。安全保障才能使这些农业干预措施真正落地。”Gbajabiamila还强调总统森林守卫倡议，根据该倡议，截至2025年12月，来自7个前线州的7,000多名人员已完成训练，以支持在犯罪团伙活动地区的安全行动。他透露，总统Tinubu已于8月指示编制《国家威胁评估》和滚动五年期《战略防务行动计划》，以改善协调工作、使安全支出与行动重点保持一致，并强化机构问责。Gbajabiamila承认，尽管政府不断增加安全投入，尼日利亚人仍持续面临绑架和暴力袭击威胁，但他表示，政府认识到，其成效最终必须以公民安全来衡量。“生活在绑架或袭击威胁中的尼日利亚人，有权依据自身安全状况评价我们。我们认识到，国家能力提升与每个社区都获得可靠保护之间仍有差距。”这位幕僚长进一步将政府的安全干预与其经济改革计划联系起来，包括取消燃油补贴、外汇结构调整和税收改革。他承认，这些改革给家庭和企业带来了相当大的压力，但坚持认为，经济生产率与安全相互依存。“收入不足的政府无法维持保护公民所需的机构。在人们无法安全工作的情况下，经济也无法创造政府所需的收入。“因此，我们不得不同时处理这两个问题，尽管转型成本已对尼日利亚家庭和企业造成相当大的压力。”这位幕僚长解释道。Gbajabiamila敦促投资者因安全状况改善而重返那些商业活动曾受干扰的地区，并认为，恢复投资将创造就业、恢复本地供应链并扩大公共收入。他向商业领袖保证，政府欢迎建设性批评和切实可行的建议，并强调，总统Tinubu正视长期结构性挑战的意愿，需要所有利益相关方持续合作。“返乡的农民和重新开业的雇主将在为家人的未来作出决定。我们共同的努力必须给他们充分理由继续前进。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都地区以及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过全平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英及更广泛的中产阶级报道，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇平台。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title: Dangote Refinery’s historic IPO nets investors from 120 countries worldwide, 54 in Africa
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其里程碑式首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自全球六个有人居住大洲120个国家的投资者申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries. In a statement on Tuesday, the company described the development as an unprecedented demonstration of the continent’s capacity to mobilise capital and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. The historic offering, widely described as The People’s IPO, achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, bringing together investors from across the continent and beyond in a transaction that could redefine the scale, accessibility and international reach of African capital markets. More than a conventional fundraising exercise, the IPO has become a landmark in financial inclusion, showing how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions, and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants. The transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation. For Dangote Industries Limited, the IPO’s conclusion marks a defining moment in its industrial journey, shifting the refinery’s ownership proposition from an investment driven by a single entrepreneurial vision to an opportunity for broader African participation. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise, and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development. “When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said. “We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. We built the refinery in Africa, through African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. “Today, we have made history together. But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs, and industrialists that this transaction inspires. Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny. As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it.” The statement said the IPO’s geographical reach is particularly significant for a continent where capital markets have historically been fragmented by national boundaries, differing regulatory environments and limited retail investor participation. By attracting applications from all 54 African countries, the transaction has shown the potential for a more connected investment ecosystem, allowing Africans to participate in major industrial opportunities beyond their domestic markets. The offering also highlights the growing importance of digital financial infrastructure in widening investment access. Through partnerships involving traditional financial institutions and technology-driven investment platforms, the transaction created multiple channels for eligible investors to express interest and submit applications. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects. “The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications from 120 countries demonstrate extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence investors place in this refinery’s future. We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said. “What makes this transaction particularly meaningful is the breadth of participation. The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents. That is a powerful endorsement of the refinery’s potential and of Africa’s growing relevance in global investment markets.” The refinery’s IPO opened on 14 September, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on 13 October, the offer was extended to 27 October after the Securities and Exchange Commission approved it, giving investors across Africa and other international markets more time to participate. The extension reflected the Group’s stated ambition to prioritise broad ownership alongside the transaction’s financial objectives. Beyond the refinery’s industrial significance, the IPO also established a model for collaboration across Africa’s financial services ecosystem. Its distribution network brought together institutions across banking, securities trading, financial technology, and investor engagement, showing how coordinated infrastructure can expand access to large-scale investment opportunities. Dangote Industries Limited Group Chief Financial Officer Murat Erden said the transaction set an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets, speaking to the offering’s execution and broader significance. “The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the continent’s growing appetite for investment. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said. “Importantly, this transaction is underpinned by exceptional industrial and financial fundamentals. With US$22.5 billion in revenue and US$5.52 billion in EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, Dangote Refinery combines world-class industrial scale, strong profitability and significant long-term growth potential. Our greatest achievement is not simply the capital we mobilise, but the doors we open and the foundation we lay for future generations of African investors, entrepreneurs and businesses. We believe the People’s IPO will be remembered not only as a landmark transaction in African capital market history, but also as a blueprint for a more inclusive, interconnected and globally competitive African financial ecosystem — one in which Africans increasingly finance, own and share in the prosperity created by their continent’s industrial transformation.” The successful conclusion of the offer comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals pursues an ambitious programme to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and support greater energy security across Africa. Located in Lagos, the refinery represents one of the continent’s largest private industrial investments and a major effort to reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products while building domestic processing capacity
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: Dangote炼油厂历史性首次公开募股吸引全球120个国家的投资者，其中54个来自非洲
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其具有里程碑意义的首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自六大有人居住洲120个国家的投资者申购申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。该公司周二发表声明称，这一进展前所未有地展现了非洲大陆调动资本、扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。此次历史性发行被广泛称为“人民IPO”，实现了对非洲100%的地域覆盖，将非洲各地乃至海外投资者汇聚到一起完成交易，可能重新定义非洲资本市场的规模、可及性和国际影响力。这次IPO不只是传统的融资活动，更成为金融普惠的里程碑，展示了数字技术、协同配合的金融机构以及创新分销渠道如何将数百万潜在投资者与过去主要由机构投资者和高净值人士主导的投资机会连接起来。此次交易得到了广泛商业银行、证券经纪公司、金融科技平台、资本市场机构和分销合作伙伴网络的支持，各方协作突破了国界限制、扩大了本次发行的参与范围，并为散户参与开辟了新路径。对丹格特集团有限公司而言，IPO的完成标志着其工业发展历程中的决定性时刻，使该炼油厂的所有权模式从依靠单一企业家愿景推动的投资，转变为更广泛的非洲投资者共同参与的机会。丹格特集团有限公司总裁兼首席执行官阿里科·丹格特表示，这一成果有力印证了非洲的信心、进取精神以及调动自身资源推动发展的能力。“当初我们着手建设这座炼油厂时，许多人怀疑如此规模的项目能否由非洲人建成。我们证明了非洲能够建设它。如今，通过这次历史性IPO，我们展示了一项同样重要的事实：非洲人已经准备好拥有并参与自身产业所创造的繁荣。“来自非洲全部54个国家的投资者提交申购申请，对我而言意义重大。这表明我们的人民不只想消费非洲生产的产品，还愿意投资并拥有这些产业，分享其未来。这就是我们始终坚信的非洲。”他说。“我们推动这次IPO并非仅仅因为需要筹集资本。我们希望打开所有权的大门，让普通非洲人有机会参与一家具有全球意义的企业，并建立一种共享繁荣的新文化。我们依靠非洲人的决心在非洲建设了这座炼油厂，它的未来也必须为非洲人创造机会。“今天，我们共同创造了历史。但更大的成就，将是这次交易激励起来的非洲投资者、创业者和实业家群体。我们的目标不只是打造成功的企业，还要帮助建设一个繁荣、自给自足的非洲，使非洲人民成为其经济命运的参与者。随着我们推进扩张计划和“2030愿景”战略，我们将继续专注于提升运营表现，深化对非洲能源安全的贡献，并打造一家能够回报投资者信任的企业。”声明称，这次IPO的地域覆盖范围尤其重要，因为非洲大陆的资本市场历来受到国界分割、监管环境差异以及散户参与度有限等因素影响。通过吸引非洲全部54个国家提交申购申请，此次交易展示了一个更加互联的投资生态所具有的潜力，使非洲人能够参与本国市场之外的重要工业投资机会。此次发行还凸显了数字金融基础设施在扩大投资可及性方面日益重要的作用。通过传统金融机构与技术驱动型投资平台之间的合作，此次交易为符合条件的投资者提供了多种表达投资意愿并提交申购申请的渠道。丹格特炼油与石化公司董事总经理兼首席执行官戴维·伯德表示，国际市场反响反映出投资者对该炼油厂运营能力、工业规模及长期增长前景的信心。“这次IPO成功完成，是丹格特炼油与石化公司的重要里程碑。来自120个国家的投资者申购申请证明，国际社会对我们的业务展现出非凡兴趣，也体现了投资者对这家炼油厂未来的信心。我们已经建成全球最具规模的炼油与石化综合体之一，当前重点仍是将这种工业规模转化为卓越运营、可持续增长和长期股东价值。”他说。“让此次交易更具意义的是广泛参与。投资者遍布非洲每一个国家以及六大有人居住洲，并有机会持有一家重要非洲工业企业的股份。这是对该炼油厂潜力以及非洲在全球投资市场中日益提升重要性的有力背书。”该炼油厂的IPO于9月14日开放认购，以每股525奈拉的价格发行41亿股普通股，拟募集资金约2.15万亿奈拉。此次发行原定于10月13日结束，但在证券交易委员会批准后延长至10月27日，为非洲及其他国际市场的投资者提供了更多参与时间。延长期限体现了集团在追求交易财务目标的同时，优先推动广泛所有权的既定愿景。除炼油厂本身的重要工业意义外，此次IPO还为非洲金融服务生态体系内的协作建立了范例。其分销网络将银行、证券交易、金融科技和投资者互动等领域的机构汇聚起来，展示了协同基础设施如何扩大公众参与大规模投资机会。丹格特集团有限公司首席财务官穆拉特·尔登表示，这次交易为非洲大陆资本市场树立了重要先例，其执行过程和广泛意义同样值得关注。“丹格特炼油厂人民IPO远不只是一次具有里程碑意义的融资活动。它标志着非洲资本市场演进过程中的决定性时刻，展现了我们大陆调动国内储蓄、连接跨境投资者以及扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。投资者覆盖120个国家，包括非洲全部54个国家，这是一项非凡成就，也是非洲大陆投资意愿日益增强的有力证明。通过汇聚银行、资本市场机构、证券经纪商、金融科技平台和创新的数字分销渠道，我们证明了非洲资本市场能够跨越国界，让数百万人获得过去难以触及的投资机会。”他说。“尤为重要的是，这次交易建立在卓越的工业和财务基本面之上。2026年前九个月，丹格特炼油厂实现225亿美元收入和55.2亿美元EBITDA，兼具世界级工业规模、强劲盈利能力及显著的长期增长潜力。我们最大的成就不仅是调动资本，更是打开大门，为未来几代非洲投资者、创业者和企业奠定基础。我们相信，人民IPO不仅会作为非洲资本市场史上的里程碑交易被铭记，也将成为建设更具包容性、更互联且具备全球竞争力的非洲金融生态的蓝图。在这个生态中，非洲人将越来越多地为自身大陆的工业转型提供资金、拥有产业，并分享其创造的繁荣。”此次发行成功完成之际，丹格特炼油与石化公司正推进一项雄心勃勃的计划，以扩大炼油和石化业务、加强分销网络，并支持提升非洲整体能源安全。该炼油厂位于拉各斯，是非洲大陆规模最大的私人工业投资之一，也是非洲为减少对进口成品油依赖、建设本土加工能力所作的重大努力。

Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police. “We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/kano.summary_zh: 卡诺州议会已批准拟议中的宪法修正案，允许各州政府建立并运营自己的警察部队。Dala表示，议员们已经审议并批准了有关建立州警察的拟议宪法审查。他说：“我们今天在全体会议上批准了关于建立州警察的宪法审查。”
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/kano.body: The Kano State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment to allow state governments to establish and operate their own police forces. The approval was confirmed by the Majority Leader of the Assembly, Lawan Hussaini Dala, shortly after plenary on Tuesday. Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police. “We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said. The approval followed deliberations on the proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which seek to give state governments the legal authority to establish and operate their own police forces. During plenary, the lawmakers considered the constitutional alteration bill in the Committee of the Whole, deliberating on clauses one to 26 of the proposed amendment. The lawmakers had earlier adopted a motion to consider the constitutional amendment bill in the Committee of the Whole before proceeding with deliberations on its provisions. https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary: The farmers carrying red flags began their march from Igatpuri to Mumbai along the Nashik–Mumbai highway. In the evening, Fadnavis met a delegation of farmers under the leadership of Ajit Nawale. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has assured farmers that the state government will extend all possible assistance to help them overcome the challenges arising from the prevailing drought conditions.
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 举着红旗的农民从伊加特普里出发，沿纳西克—孟买公路向孟买行进。傍晚， Fadnavis会见了由阿吉特·纳瓦莱带领的农民代表团。 Maharashtra首席部长德夫德拉· Fadnavis向农民保证，州政府将提供一切可能的援助，帮助他们克服当前干旱状况带来的挑战。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: The farmers carrying red flags began their march from Igatpuri to Mumbai along the Nashik–Mumbai highway. All India Kisan Sabha leader Ajit Nawale called for reform in the farm loan waiver policy. He argued that farmers who regularly repay their loans should benefit from the scheme. In the evening, Fadnavis met a delegation of farmers under the leadership of Ajit Nawale. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has assured farmers that the state government will extend all possible assistance to help them overcome the challenges arising from the prevailing drought conditions. Fadnavis emphasised that the government was committed to reducing the hardships faced by farming families through financial assistance, drinking water arrangements, fodder supplies and measures to strengthen agricultural support systems. The Chief Minister announced that pending instalments under the Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana would be paid to eligible farmers. He also assured that the government will consider demand for increasing the ₹ 50,000 incentive provided to farmers who regularly repay their crop loans. "A ministerial group constituted to examine farm loan waivers will discuss the proposal to increase the incentive. A suitable decision will be taken after considering the state's financial position," said Fadnavis. Fadnavis also ordered officials to expedite the release of pending instalments under the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana for women beneficiaries who have completed their e-KYC verification. The Chief Minister said Maharashtra was among the leading states in terms of the number of women receiving benefits under such welfare schemes. The Chief Minister directed the concerned department to examine the possibility of restoring the triggers previously used under the crop insurance scheme. The state government has expressed a positive view on increasing the monthly honorarium of school nutrition programme workers. These workers currently receive ₹ 2,500 per month, and the proposal under consideration would raise their honorarium by ₹ 1,000 to ₹ 3,500 per month. After the assurance, Ajit Nawale announced the decision to withdraw Long March. "CM Fadnavis responded positively to our demands. So we have decided to withdraw the Long March." said Nawale. The meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Water Resources Minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan, Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne and MLA Vinod Nikole
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: Fadnavis政府承诺提供旱灾援助后，农民取消前往孟买的游行 101793121495093
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 举着红旗的农民从伊加特普里出发，沿纳西克—孟买公路向孟买行进。全印度农民协会领导人阿杰特·纳瓦勒呼吁改革农业贷款减免政策。他认为 regularly 偿还贷款的农民应当从该计划中受益。傍晚，法德纳维斯会见了由阿杰特·纳瓦勒带领的农民代表团。马哈拉施特拉邦首席部长德文德拉·法德纳维斯向农民保证，邦政府将提供一切可能的援助，帮助他们克服当前干旱状况带来的挑战。法德纳维斯强调，政府致力于通过财政援助、饮用水供应、饲料供应以及加强农业支持体系的措施，减轻农业家庭面临的困难。首席部长宣布，符合条件的农民将获得“Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana”计划下待发放的款项。他还保证，政府将考虑提高向 regularly 偿还作物贷款农民提供的 ₹ 50,000 奖励金额。“为研究农业贷款减免而成立的部长级小组将讨论提高奖励金额的提议。在考虑邦财政状况后，将作出适当决定。”法德纳维斯说。法德纳维斯还命令官员加快向已完成电子身份验证的女性受益人发放“Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana”计划下的待拨款项。首席部长表示，马哈拉施特拉邦是此类福利计划女性受益人数最多的邦之一。首席部长指示相关部门研究恢复此前在农作物保险计划中使用的触发条件。邦政府对提高学校营养计划工作人员的月度酬金持积极态度。这些工作人员目前每月获得 ₹ 2,500，正在考虑的提议将把其酬金提高 ₹ 1,000，达到每月 ₹ 3,500。在获得保证后，阿杰特·纳瓦勒宣布撤回长march行动。“首席部长法德纳维斯积极回应了我们的要求。因此，我们决定撤回长march行动。”纳瓦勒说。出席会议的还有副首席部长埃克纳特·辛德、努内特拉·阿杰特·帕瓦尔，水资源部长拉德哈克里希纳·维赫·帕蒂尔、水资源部长吉里什·马哈詹、财政部长钱德拉谢卡尔·巴万库勒、农业部长达塔特雷·巴尔内以及议员维诺德·尼科莱

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.title: US Visa Bond: Full list of countries, including Nigeria, required to pay up to $20,000
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.summary: Layer 1 The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.summary_zh: 据美国国务院消息，美国已将50个国家的公民列入名单。这些公民申请某些访问签证时，必须缴纳最高20,000美元的签证保证金，尼日利亚位列其中。国务院在2026年10月2日发布的通知中列出了适用签证保证金计划的国家及其各自实施日期。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.body: Layer 1 The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. The measure applies to eligible applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas travelling on passports issued by the listed countries. The bond amounts are $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000, with the specific amount determined by a consular officer during the visa interview. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates. The programme operates under Section 221(g)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, with the department stating that the requirement applies regardless of where an applicant submits their visa application. The 50 countries listed by the US Department of State, alongside their implementation dates, are: Nigerian citizens applying for B-1 business or B-2 tourist visas may be required to post a bond of $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000 if they are otherwise eligible for the visa. The amount is determined during the visa interview. The bond is an additional financial requirement and does not guarantee that the applicant will receive a visa. Applicants must submit Department of Homeland Security Form I-352 and agree to the bond’s terms through the US Department of the Treasury’s Pay.gov platform. The department warns applicants not to pay a bond before being instructed to do so by a consular officer. Applicants are expected to use the specific payment link supplied through official instructions. The bond may be paid by the applicant or a third party, such as a relative, friend or business associate. However, the name of the person identified as the bond obligor on Form I-352 must match the name of the person making the payment. If the bond conditions are satisfied, the money is refundable under the programme’s terms. The programme also imposes travel conditions on people who post visa bonds. According to the State Department, bond holders must enter and leave the United States through designated commercial air ports of entry, including US Customs and Border Protection preclearance locations. They are not permitted to use charter aircraft, general aviation, land borders or sea ports of entry under the stated bond conditions. Failure to comply with the designated entry and exit requirements could result in problems with entry or the recording of a traveller’s departure. The department outlined several circumstances under which a bond may be cancelled and the deposit returned automatically. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.title_zh: 美国签证保证金：包括尼日利亚在内的完整国家名单及最高2万美元缴费规定
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.body_zh:
第一层：美国国务院表示，美国已列出50个国家，其公民申请特定访问签证时须缴纳最高20,000美元的签证保证金，其中包括尼日利亚。

这项措施适用于持有所列国家签发的护照、申请B-1商务签证或B-2旅游签证且符合资格的申请人。

保证金金额为10,000美元、15,000美元或20,000美元，具体金额由领事官员在签证面谈期间确定。

美国国务院在2026年10月2日发布的通知中列出了适用签证保证金计划的国家及其各自的实施日期。

该计划依据《移民和国籍法》第221(g)(3)条实施。国务院表示，无论申请人在何处递交签证申请，均须遵守这一要求。

美国国务院列出的50个国家及其实施日期如下：

尼日利亚公民申请B-1商务签证或B-2旅游签证时，如符合签证的其他资格条件，可能须缴纳10,000美元、15,000美元或20,000美元的保证金。

具体金额将在签证面谈期间确定。

保证金是一项额外的财务要求，并不保证申请人一定获发签证。

申请人必须提交美国国土安全部I-352表格，并通过美国财政部的Pay.gov平台同意保证金条款。

国务院提醒申请人，在领事官员指示缴纳保证金之前不得付款。

申请人应使用官方指引提供的专用付款链接。

保证金可由申请人本人或亲属、朋友、商业伙伴等第三方支付。

但是，I-352表格中被列为保证金义务人的姓名必须与付款人的姓名一致。

如果满足保证金条件，款项可依照该计划的规定退还。

该计划还对缴纳签证保证金的人施加旅行条件。

据国务院称，保证金缴纳者必须从指定的商业航空入境口岸入境并离境，包括美国海关与边境保护局预先清关地点。

根据规定的保证金条件，他们不得使用包机、一般航空、陆路边境或海港入境口岸。

未遵守指定入境和离境要求可能导致入境受阻，或影响旅行者离境记录的登记。

国务院列举了若干可以取消保证金并自动退还押金的情形。

本文所发表的意见不代表《Vanguard》报或该报任何员工的观点。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title: Lawmakers move to make formal identification compulsory for renting apartments in Abuja
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary: The Senate on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, to present valid means of identification before renting apartments as part of efforts to curb criminal activities.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary_zh: 参议院周二决定启动立法，要求联邦首都 Territory（FCT）阿布贾的租户在租赁公寓前出示有效身份证件，以协助遏制犯罪活动。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: The Senate on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, to present valid means of identification before renting apartments as part of efforts to curb criminal activities. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio , directed the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, to draft the bill for consideration by the National Assembly. Mr Akpabio gave the directive during the plenary while lawmakers were debating a report by the Senate committees on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations; Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters; Foreign Affairs; and Special Duties on the need to protect Nigerians from being trafficked to Libya for slavery. The report was presented by Aniekan Bassey, chair of the Senate Committee on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations. Mr Akpabio expressed concern that many property owners rent out their properties to strangers without obtaining adequate information about their identities, occupations and other relevant details. He argued that the lack of proper documentation makes it difficult for security agencies to trace suspects when crimes are committed, allowing perpetrators to escape without leaving a clear trail. “A lot of people just give their properties to strangers. They don’t even have any papers to know where they come from. In some instances, the phone number that is used in renting the property does not even belong to the occupant of the house. So when something happens, the person will escape and then leave no trace,” he said. The Senate President urged Mr Bamidele to consider legislation that would strengthen tenancy regulations and make landlords more accountable for verifying prospective tenants’ identities. “People enter people’s properties with very nefarious intentions and, at the end of the day, they will just commit some crimes, traffic people’s children and make money while living in the house itself. It is something that we must tighten the laws on tenancy,” he said. Mr Akpabio proposed adopting an approach similar to the banking sector’s Know Your Customer (KYC) policy, which requires financial institutions to verify customers’ identities. “As you know in the bank, they say, know your customer; this one we can say, know your tenants. Let’s make the necessary law for the FCT, for instance. We can enact an Act for the FCT that says know your tenants so that nobody will come and live in the house and perpetrate crime,” he said. He said the proposed legislation could also cover the rental of shops and other commercial spaces, arguing that inadequate identity verification could expose occupants and business owners to criminal attacks. Mr Akpabio said people renting shops should provide verifiable identification, including a driver’s licence or international passport, to help security agencies trace them if they are implicated in criminal activities. He said the lack of reliable tenant information could leave property owners unable to identify or help locate people who used their premises to commit crimes. “And then even those that are going to do shoplets, we can use that opportunity to regulate shoplets because people go into secluded environments and then do shoplets, and then they move in and they rob them in the night and escape. To support his argument, Mr Akpabio recalled measures his administration introduced to tackle kidnapping when he was governor of Akwa Ibom State. He said his government prescribed the death penalty for kidnapping and introduced measures involving the destruction of property used as hideouts by criminals. The Senate President noted that the measures encouraged landlords to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious behaviour for fear of losing them. He said similar measures could help deter criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as bases for criminal activities. If enacted as envisaged by the Senate President, the proposed legislation would require landlords in the FCT to verify prospective tenants’ identities before letting out their property. The proposal is intended to help security agencies trace people suspected of committing crimes from their residential addresses and discourage criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as hideouts. However, its effectiveness would depend on the legislation’s details, including how identities would be verified, what records landlords would be required to keep, and how compliance would be monitored. If enacted, the law could make it easier for investigators to establish the identities of tenants linked to rented property. It could also impose additional responsibilities on landlords and property agents, potentially requiring them to retain identification records and provide relevant information to authorised authorities when legally required. The proposal could, however, raise concerns about privacy, the security of tenants’ personal information and the possibility of landlords using the requirement to discriminate against prospective tenants or deny accommodation to people who cannot readily provide the prescribed documents. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 provides a framework for lawful, secure handling of personal information. Any system requiring landlords to collect and retain tenants’ identification details would need to comply with applicable data protection obligations. The proposal remains in the drafting stage, based on the proceedings described by the Senate President. It would need to go through the legislative process before becoming law
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title_zh: 议员推动将正式身份证明设为在阿布贾租住公寓的必备条件
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body_zh: 参议院周二决定启动立法，要求联邦首都领地的租户在租赁阿布贾公寓前出示有效身份证明，以遏制犯罪活动。参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿卡皮奥指示参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱起草法案，供国民议会审议。阿卡皮奥先生在议员们讨论参议院各委员会关于保护尼日利亚人免遭拐运至利比亚沦为奴隶的报告时下达了该指示。相关委员会包括侨民与非政府组织委员会，司法、人权与法律事务委员会，外交委员会以及特别职责委员会。报告由参议院侨民与非政府组织委员会主席阿尼坎·巴西提交。阿卡皮奥先生表示担忧，许多房东在未充分了解租户身份、职业及其他相关信息的情况下，便将房产出租给陌生人。他认为，缺少适当文件会使安全机构在犯罪发生后难以追查嫌疑人，让作案者逃脱且不留下明确线索。他说：“很多人直接把房产交给陌生人。他们甚至没有任何文件可以证明租户来自哪里。在某些情况下，租房时留下的电话号码甚至不属于房屋实际居住者。因此，一旦发生事情，那个人就会逃走，并且不会留下任何痕迹。”参议院议长敦促巴米德莱先生考虑制定法律，加强租赁监管，并促使房东对核实潜在租户身份承担更多责任。他说：“有人怀着极其恶劣的意图进入他人的房产，最终实施犯罪、拐卖他人的children，从中获利，同时还住在房子里。对于租赁问题，我们必须收紧法律。”阿卡皮奥先生提议采用类似银行业“了解你的客户”（KYC）政策的做法，该政策要求金融机构核实客户身份。他说：“正如你们所知，银行会要求‘了解你的客户’；对于这件事，我们可以说‘了解你的租户’。例如，我们可以为联邦首都领地制定必要的法律。我们可以为联邦首都领地颁布一项规定，要求‘了解你的租户’，这样就不会有人入住房屋并实施犯罪。”他说，拟议立法也可涵盖商店及其他商业场所的租赁，并认为身份核验不足可能使占用者和商户遭受犯罪袭击。阿卡皮奥先生说，租用商店的人应提供可核实的身份证明，包括驾驶证或国际护照，以便在涉嫌犯罪时帮助安全机构追踪他们。他说，缺乏可靠的租户信息，可能导致房东无法识别或协助寻找利用其场所实施犯罪的人。他还说：“对于那些要租用小商铺的人，我们也可以借此监管小商铺，因为人们会进入偏僻场所经营小商铺，随后在夜间实施抢劫并逃走。”为支持自己的论点，阿卡皮奥先生提到其担任阿夸伊博姆州州长时为打击绑架而采取的措施。他说，其政府规定对绑架行为处以死刑，并推出措施，摧毁犯罪分子用作藏身点的房产。参议院议长指出，这些措施促使房东留意其场所内的活动，并因担心失去房产而报告可疑行为。他说，类似措施也有助于阻止犯罪分子把出租公寓和商业场所当作犯罪活动据点。如果按照参议院议长的设想颁布，拟议立法将要求联邦首都领地的房东在出租房产前核实潜在租户身份。该提案旨在帮助安全机构根据住址追踪涉嫌犯罪的人员，并阻止犯罪分子将出租公寓和商业场所作为藏身点。然而，其成效将取决于法律的具体条款，包括如何核实身份、房东须保存哪些记录，以及如何监督合规情况。法律若获颁布，调查人员将更容易确认与出租房产有关联的租户身份。该法律还可能对房东和房地产中介施加额外责任，或要求他们保留身份证明记录，并在法律要求时向获授权机关提供相关信息。不过，该提案也可能引发对隐私、租户个人信息安全以及房东利用该要求歧视潜在租户或拒绝向无法迅速提供规定文件者提供住所的担忧。《尼日利亚数据保护法》2023为合法、安全处理个人信息提供了框架。任何要求房东收集并保存租户身份信息的系统，都必须遵守适用的数据保护义务。根据参议院议长所述的会议进展，该提案目前仍处于起草阶段，须经过立法程序才能成为法律

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/jiga.body: The Jigawa State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking the establishment of state police in Nigeria. The Speaker of the House, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, announced the approval during plenary, saying the move was aimed at strengthening community policing and improving security across the country. He explained that the proposed amendment was transmitted to the state Assembly for consideration after its passage by the Senate and the House of Representatives. According to him, the establishment of state police would help address security challenges at the grassroots by giving state governments greater responsibility for protecting lives and property. The approval is part of ongoing efforts to decentralise Nigeria’s policing system and strengthen the capacity of states to respond to security threats within their jurisdictions. The development comes after the National Assembly gave state Houses of Assembly a 30-day deadline to communicate their positions on the proposed constitutional amendment. State legislatures were directed to indicate whether they supported or opposed the bill as part of the constitutional amendment process. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/jiga.title_zh: 贾加瓦州议会批准设立州警察的宪法修正案
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/jiga.body_zh: 尼日利亚吉加瓦州议会已批准拟议的宪法修正案，寻求在尼日利亚建立州警察。州议会议长哈鲁纳·阿里尤·丹雅廷在全会上宣布了这一批准，称此举旨在加强社区警务并改善全国安全状况。他解释道，参议院和众议院通过拟议修正案后，将其提交州议会审议。根据他的说法，建立州警察将使州政府在保护生命和财产方面承担更大责任，从而有助于解决基层的安全挑战。此次批准是尼日利亚推进警务权力下放、加强各州应对其管辖范围内安全威胁能力的一系列工作之一。此前，尼日利亚国民议会要求各州议会在30天内就是否支持拟议宪法修正案表明立场。州立法机构被告知，作为宪法修正案程序的一部分，应明确表示支持或反对该法案。此处表达的意见不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的观点

https://leadership.ng/reps-demand-regula.summary_zh: 因此，众议院敦促联邦政府为电动汽车、压缩天然气汽车及相关清洁出行设备的商业进口建立透明的许可和审批框架。提出该动议时，他指出，作为尼日利亚能源转型和经济多元化议程的一部分，尼日利亚已经采取了促进向电动汽车、压缩天然气汽车、液化石油气汽车及其他清洁交通技术转型的政策。
https://leadership.ng/reps-demand-regula.body: Consequently, the House urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing and approval framework for the commercial importation of EVs, CNG vehicles and related clean mobility equipment. It asked the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), and other relevant agencies, to develop objective qualification criteria for import approval. These resolutions were a result of the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Ademorin Aliu Kuye(APC, Lagos) at plenary on Tuesday. Moving the motion, he noted that Nigeria had adopted policies promoting the transition to EVs, CNG vehicles, Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) vehicles, and other clean transportation technologies as part of its energy transition and economic diversification agenda. According to him, Nigeria has the opportunity to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation, and domestic value addition by linking import incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity. It further asked the Federal Government to align tax incentives, import duty concessions, and other fiscal benefits with compliance with this regulatory framework to promote sustained investment in local infrastructure. The House mandated the Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment, and Legislative Compliance to monitor implementation and report within four weeks for legislative action. https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.body: Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement in the North-Central region, made this known on Tuesday while speaking with State House correspondents at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. She explained that the President receives regular briefings on the living conditions of Nigerians through community engagement activities and members of the Federal Executive Council. “I don’t feel it’s only media people who understand what the people are facing. Some of the realities our people are experiencing are what we communicate to Mr President,” she said. Essiet further stressed that the regular briefings keep Tinubu informed about the cost of basic commodities. “I usually tell people, you think Mr President doesn’t know the price of egg or bread in the market? He does, because we brief him regularly, and so do members of the Federal Executive Council,” she stated. Regarding infrastructure development, the presidential aide cited the planned reconstruction of the Mokwa-Bida road in Niger State as an example of efforts to address residents’ concerns. She said the road had remained in poor condition for decades, with residents repeatedly calling on the Federal Government to intervene. According to her, the road was last reconstructed 46 years ago, and its deteriorating condition has contributed to fatal accidents involving motorists and heavy-duty vehicles. “The last time that road was given out on contract was 46 years ago. So tell me if that is not the wish of the people,” she said. Essiet also disclosed that Tinubu had directed that the road be reconstructed with reinforced concrete rather than conventional asphalt to improve its durability. “Mr President said they should award the contract and make sure that the contract will be reinforced concrete, not just asphalt,” she added. Meanwhile, Vice President Kashim Shettima expressed optimism on October 19 that food prices would decline in the coming weeks, citing Federal Government efforts to address challenges affecting agricultural production. Shettima made the remarks at a forum titled Together Till 2027: An Evening with Original City Boy , organised by the City Boy Movement alongside the Relax-Tinubu-Is-Fixing-Nigeria movement, both of which support Tinubu’s re-election bid. https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.title_zh: 总统助理称，蒂努布了解鸡蛋和面包的价格
https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.body_zh: 总统负责北部和中部分地区社区互动的特别助理高级顾问Essiet周二在阿布贾总统别墅接受国家宫记者采访时透露了这一情况。她解释说，总统通过社区互动活动以及联邦执行委员会成员定期了解尼日利亚人的生活状况。她说：“我不认为只有媒体人士了解民众正在面临的困境。我们向总统先生传达了民众正在经历的一些现实情况。”Essiet进一步强调，定期简报让Tinubu了解基本商品的价格。她说：“我通常会告诉人们，你们以为总统先生不知道市场上鸡蛋或面包的价格吗？他知道，因为我们定期向他汇报，联邦执行委员会成员也这样做。”在基础设施发展方面，这名总统助理以计划重建尼日利亚州Mokwa-Bida公路为例，说明政府为回应居民诉求所作的努力。她说，这条公路几十年来一直状况不佳，居民多次呼吁联邦政府介入。据她介绍，这条公路最后一次重建是在46年前，此后不断恶化的路况已导致涉及小汽车和重型车辆的车祸死亡。她说：“那条公路最后一次承包出去是在46年前。所以你告诉我，这难道不是民众的愿望吗？”Essiet还透露，Tinubu已指示采用钢筋混凝土而非传统沥青重建该公路，以提高其耐久性。她补充道：“总统先生说，应该把合同承包出去，并确保工程采用钢筋混凝土，而不只是沥青。”与此同时，副总统Kashim Shettima于10月19日对食品价格将在未来几周下降表示乐观，并提到联邦政府正在努力解决影响农业生产的问题。Shettimi是在一场题为《共同奋斗至2027年：与Original City Boy共度夜晚》的论坛上作出上述表态的。该论坛由City Boy Movement与Relax-Tinubu-Is-Fixing-Nigeria movement共同组织，这两个组织都支持Tinubu竞选连任。我们掌握独家优势。获取实时报道、突发新闻和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候更新 →

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/adc-.body: The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has urged the National Assembly to reject President Bola Tinubu’s proposed $20 billion and £1 billion foreign borrowing unless the Federal Government provides full details of the facilities and demonstrates their benefits to Nigerians. The council said the fresh borrowing would add to the burden on Nigerians already battling rising living costs and increased taxation, questioning why the government was seeking more loans without accounting for previous borrowings and savings from fuel subsidy removal. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC faulted the administration’s borrowing plans, demanding evidence that the funds would translate into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives. “What exactly is President Tinubu borrowing all this money for? Where are the roads, the electricity, the hospitals, the jobs and the critical infrastructure that should justify this relentless accumulation of debt? Nigerians deserve answers,” Ologbondiyan said. He questioned why the government was returning to international creditors while millions of Nigerians struggled to survive the effects of its economic policies. The council warned that continued borrowing without transparent spending and measurable returns could deepen Nigeria’s debt burden, restrict future governments’ policy options and threaten the country’s economic sovereignty. “This is not a sustainable path to national development. It is a dangerous attempt to mortgage the future of Nigeria and generations yet unborn,” Ologbondiyan said. The ADC-PCC demanded that Tinubu publish a comprehensive account of all domestic and foreign borrowing since May 29, 2023, including a breakdown of revenue realised from subsidy removal and how the funds had been spent. It also called for full disclosure of the proposed loans’ purposes, interest rates, repayment periods, fees, conditions and any collateral or guarantees attached to the facilities. “Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of poor economic management. Borrowing must be tied to clearly defined national priorities, transparent expenditure and measurable outcomes. Anything less is an injustice to the Nigerian people,” the council said. It urged lawmakers to insist on accountability and refuse to approve the facilities until the Federal Government establishes their necessity, sustainability and tangible benefits to Nigerians. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/adc-.title_zh: ADC-PCC致函国民议会：因缺乏透明度，拒绝Tinubu的210亿美元贷款
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/adc-.body_zh: 非洲民主大会全国竞选委员会（ADC-PCC）敦促国民议会否决总统博拉·蒂努布拟议的200亿美元和10亿英镑外债，除非联邦政府提供这些融资安排的完整细节，并向尼日利亚人民证明其益处。该委员会表示，新一轮借款将加重尼日利亚民众的负担；他们已在应对生活成本上涨和税收增加带来的压力。委员会质疑，在未说明此前借款情况以及取消燃料补贴所节省资金去向的情况下，政府为何还要寻求更多贷款。ADC-PCC媒体与公共事务主任科拉·奥洛格博迪扬在一份声明中批评政府的借款计划，要求提供证据，证明这些资金将切实改善公民的生活。奥洛格博迪扬说：“蒂努布总统究竟借这么多钱做什么？那些本应为持续累积债务提供理由的道路、电力、医院、就业岗位和关键基础设施在哪里？尼日利亚人民有权得到答案。”他质疑，在数百万尼日利亚人仍在艰难应对其经济政策影响之际，政府为何要重新向国际债权人借款。该委员会警告，在缺乏透明支出和可衡量回报的情况下持续借款，可能加深尼日利亚的债务负担，限制未来政府的政策选择，并威胁国家经济主权。奥洛格博迪扬说：“这不是通往国家发展的可持续道路，而是企图拿尼日利亚的未来以及尚未出生世代的未来作抵押的危险做法。”ADC-PCC要求蒂努布公布自2023年5月29日以来所有国内外借款的综合账目，包括取消补贴所得收入的明细，以及这些资金的支出情况。该委员会还要求全面披露拟议贷款的用途、利率、偿还期限、费用、附带条件，以及融资安排涉及的任何抵押或担保。该委员会说：“尼日利亚不能靠借款摆脱经济管理不善。借款必须与明确界定的国家优先事项、透明的支出和可衡量的成果相挂钩。任何低于这一要求的行为，都是对尼日利亚人民的不公。”该委员会敦促议员坚持问责，在联邦政府证明有关融资安排的必要性、可持续性及其对尼日利亚人民的切实益处之前，拒绝批准这些融资安排。本文所载评论不代表Vanguard报纸及其任何员工的观点

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea this year are estimated to have already set an all-time annual record, the culture ministry said Tuesday. Preliminary figures from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism showed that this year's arrivals reached about 18.91 million through Monday, and the total is believed to have surpassed the previous annual record of 18.94 million, set last year, Tuesday, with more than two months left in the year. The ministry expects about 1.94 million people to visit next month if the current trend continues, with the annual total topping 20 million for the first time in the third week of November. Visitor numbers rose across most major markets, including Chinese-speaking regions, Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe and the Americas. Growth is also spreading beyond Seoul, with more foreign tourists entering the country through regional airports and ports and visiting areas outside the capital, a trend Chae described as "very encouraging." "We will focus not only on quantitative expansion but also on strengthening quality so that Korea can firmly establish itself as an irreplaceable travel destination in the global tourism market," Chae said in a press release. Foreign visitors' spending also jumped 47.7 percent from a year earlier, driven mainly by shopping, accommodation, and medical and wellness services. The government attributed the record numbers to the global popularity of Korean pop culture, innovation by the tourism industry and public hospitality toward foreign visitors

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.summary_zh: 总统博拉·蒂努布已向参议院提交一项法案，请求授权尼日利亚政府与其他国家达成协议，将已定罪的尼日利亚公民移交至尼日利亚服刑。该法案拟修订《2004年已定罪罪犯移交法及实施法》，以便根据双方协议促进尼日利亚与其他国家之间移交已定罪罪犯。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.body: President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill to the Senate seeking to empower the Nigerian government to enter into agreements with other countries for the transfer of convicted Nigerian citizens to serve their sentences in Nigeria. The bill seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, 2004, to facilitate the transfer of convicted offenders between Nigeria and other countries under mutual agreements. Mr Tinubu transmitted the bill to the Senate in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday. In the letter, the president said the proposed legislation would empower the Nigerian government to enter into agreements with other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders to Nigeria. He also said the legislation would enable Nigeria to honour similar requests from foreign governments, subject to the terms of the agreements. He added that the bill would empower the president, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to apply the law to any country with which Nigeria had entered into such an agreement. According to him, this would facilitate the implementation of agreements with countries outside the Commonwealth. After reading the president’s letter, Mr Akpabio referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative consideration. Nigeria has had several cases involving public officials and political figures convicted by foreign courts. Among them is former Delta State Governor James Ibori, who was sentenced to 13 years in prison in the United Kingdom in 2012 after pleading guilty to money laundering offences. He was released in 2016. Former Deputy Senate President Ike Ekweremadu was sentenced to nine years and eight months in prison in the UK in 2023 for his role in an organ-trafficking conspiracy involving a young man. Similarly, Abidemi Rufai, a former aide to Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, was sentenced to five years in prison in the United States in 2022 for wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. Nigeria and the United Kingdom already have a prisoner-transfer agreement that provides for eligible prisoners to serve their sentences in their home countries, subject to the applicable conditions and the agreement of both governments. The proposed amendment seeks to provide a legal framework for implementing prisoner-transfer agreements with countries outside the Commonwealth. However, the proposed legislation would not automatically entitle every Nigerian convicted abroad to be transferred home, as eligibility would depend on the relevant agreement and its conditions
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.title_zh: 920714 蒂努布向参议院提交法案，允许将境外已定罪的尼日利亚人移交回国
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.body_zh: 尼日利亚总统博拉·蒂努布已向参议院提交一项法案，寻求授权尼日利亚政府与其他国家达成协议，将已定罪的尼日利亚公民移交至尼日利亚服刑。该法案拟修订《2004年已定罪犯移交法及实施法》，以便根据双方协议，在尼日利亚与其他国家之间移交已定罪犯。蒂努布先生周二在参议院全体会议上通过参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿卡皮奥宣读的一封信，将法案提交参议院。总统在信中表示，拟议立法将授权尼日利亚政府与其他国家达成协议，将已定罪犯移交至尼日利亚。他还表示，该立法将使尼日利亚能够根据协议条款，满足外国政府提出的类似请求。他补充说，法案将授权总统通过在《联邦公报》上发布命令，将该法适用于与尼日利亚达成此类协议的任何国家。据他所说，这将有助于实施与英联邦以外国家达成的协议。阿卡皮奥先生宣读总统信件后，将法案提交参议院规则与事务委员会作进一步立法审议。尼日利亚已发生多起涉及被外国法院定罪的公职人员和政治人物的案件。其中包括前三角洲州州长詹姆斯·伊博里，他于2012年在英国承认洗钱罪行后被判处13年监禁，并于2016年获释。前参议院副议长艾克·埃克韦马杜因参与涉及一名年轻男子的人体器官贩运阴谋，于2023年在英国被判处9年8个月监禁。同样，奥贡州州长达波·阿比奥杜恩的前助手阿比德米·鲁法伊因电汇欺诈和加重身份盗窃，于2022年被美国判处5年监禁。尼日利亚与英国已签署囚犯移交协议，规定符合条件的囚犯可在其本国服刑，但须遵守适用条件并获得两国政府同意。拟议修正案旨在为实施与英联邦以外国家达成的囚犯移交协议提供法律框架。不过，拟议立法并不会自动赋予所有在海外被定罪的尼日利亚人回国服刑的权利，其资格取决于相关协议及其条件

https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body: The call came during a panel discussion at a breakout session of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday. Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, Senator John Owan Enoh, said the informal nature of many small businesses remained a major barrier to accessing financing. He said some enterprises had struggled to meet documentation requirements for intervention funds, including the N5 billion MSME component of the N200 billion intervention fund. He urged measures to encourage business registration and formalisation, while calling for stronger capacity-building to enable small businesses to access credit and participate in the formal economy. Enoh also said the Federal Government was working to connect MSMEs with larger manufacturers to create more dependable supply opportunities and deepen their participation in industrial value chains. He further called for an updated census of MSMEs, noting that the current estimate of 39 million enterprises was based on 2020 data and no longer reflected present realities. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FirstBank, Olusegun Alebiosu, said improving MSME access to finance required a coordinated approach involving commercial banks, microfinance banks, development finance institutions and government. Alebiosu, represented by his Technical Adviser, Akinsope Roberts, said FirstBank had introduced financing products for businesses, including women-owned enterprises and traders. He, however, stressed that access to credit still depended on business viability and cash flow. He said the bank’s FirstCredit product had disbursed more than N1 trillion since its introduction about six years ago. According to him, the facility provides short-term working capital, with some customers borrowing for three to five days to meet immediate stock and supply needs. Alebiosu said MSMEs required different financing arrangements depending on their size and stage of development, adding that the needs of petty traders and micro-enterprises differed from those of larger businesses. He called for closer coordination between financial institutions and government to ensure that credit reached businesses through appropriate products and repayment structures. Economic Adviser to the Katsina State Governor, Khalil Nur Khalil, said governments needed to improve access to finance, training, capacity building and infrastructure to support MSME development. Khalil identified reliable data, policy alignment, public-private partnerships and business-environment reforms as critical to improving the operating conditions of small businesses. He said accurate data would help governments identify businesses, understand their financing and operational needs, and design suitable policies. He also called for better coordination among federal, state and local government policies, particularly to align industrial development strategies with MSME support programmes. Managing director of Prothrive (GrandLos PAP), Oluyemisi Obe, called for financing schemes and support programmes that reflect the changing needs of businesses as they expand. She said some MSMEs outgrew the financing initially provided to them but continued to face limitations because intervention programmes did not adequately address their growth. Obe cited her experience with the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund, which provided her business with a N5 million loan in 2016, saying the business had since expanded beyond the initial financing level. She urged policymakers to conduct gap analyses to identify the needs of businesses at different stages of development and ensure that support programmes evolved alongside them. Obe also advocated legislation at federal and state levels to provide a lasting policy framework for MSME development and reduce policy disruption caused by changes in administration. A Professor of International Studies at the Graduate School of International Management, Gaku Funabashi, called for an MSME development strategy tailored to Nigeria’s economic conditions rather than the wholesale adoption of policies from other countries. He said policymakers should identify priority industries and determine the products and components MSMEs could supply to support their development. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/federal-government.title_zh: 联邦政府与专家寻求改善微型、中型和小型企业融资框架
https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body_zh: 这通电话是在周一于阿布贾举行的第32届尼日利亚经济峰会分组会议专题讨论期间打来的。工业、贸易与投资部国务部长、参议员约翰·奥万·埃诺赫表示，许多小企业的非正规经营性质仍是获得融资的主要障碍。他说，一些企业难以满足干预资金的文件要求，其中包括2000亿奈拉干预基金下的50亿奈拉中小企业组成部分。他敦促采取措施鼓励企业注册和正规化，同时呼吁加强能力建设，使小企业能够获得信贷并参与正规经济。埃诺赫还表示，联邦政府正在努力将中小企业与大型制造商连接起来，以创造更可靠的供应机会，并加深其对产业价值链的参与。他还呼吁更新中小企业普查数据，并指出目前估计的3900万家企业采用的是2020年的数据，已无法反映当前实际情况。FirstBank董事总经理兼首席执行官奥卢塞贡·阿莱比奥苏表示，改善中小企业获得融资的情况，需要商业银行、微型金融机构、开发金融机构和政府采取协调一致的行动。阿莱比奥苏由技术顾问阿金索佩·罗伯茨代表出席。他说，FirstBank已推出面向企业的融资产品，其中包括女性拥有的企业和贸易商。然而，他强调，获得信贷仍取决于企业的可行性和现金流。他说，该银行的FirstCredit产品自约六年前推出以来，已发放超过1万亿奈拉。据他介绍，该信贷安排提供短期营运资金，一些客户借款期为3至5天，以满足即时备货和供应需求。阿莱比奥苏表示，中小企业需要根据其规模和发展阶段采用不同的融资安排，小商贩和微型企业的需求与较大企业不同。他呼吁金融机构与政府加强协调，确保企业能够通过适当的产品和还款结构获得信贷。卡塔萨州州长的经济顾问哈利勒·努尔·哈利勒表示，政府需要改善融资获取渠道，并加强培训、能力建设和基础设施，以支持中小企业发展。哈利勒指出，可靠的数据、政策协调一致、公私伙伴关系以及营商环境改革，是改善小企业经营环境的关键。他说，准确的数据将有助于政府识别企业、了解其融资和运营需求，并制定适当的政策。他还呼吁加强联邦、州和地方政府政策之间的协调，尤其是推动工业发展战略与中小企业支持计划相互衔接。Prothrive（GrandLos PAP）董事总经理奥卢耶米西·奥贝呼吁推出能够反映企业扩张过程中需求变化的融资方案和支持计划。她说，一些中小企业的规模已经超过最初获得的融资规模，但由于干预计划未能充分满足其成长需求，它们仍面临限制。奥贝提到她与拉各斯州就业信托基金合作的经验，该基金于2016年向她家企业提供了500万奈拉贷款，如今该企业的发展规模已远超初始融资水平。她敦促政策制定者开展差距分析，识别处于不同发展阶段企业的需求，并确保支持计划随企业一同演进。奥贝还主张在联邦和州层面制定法律，为中小企业发展提供持久的政策框架，并减少政府换届造成的政策中断。国际管理研究生院国际研究教授加库·舟桥山呼吁制定符合尼日利亚经济状况的中小企业发展战略，而不是全盘照搬其他国家的政策。他说，政策制定者应确定重点行业，并明确中小企业能够供应哪些产品和支持性零部件，以促进其发展。我们掌握最新动态。获取实时报道、独家爆料和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp频道，随时随地获取最新消息 →

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/health/he.body: The federal government is partnering with a US-based organisation, Operation End Starvation, to mobilise more than $1 billion to combat child malnutrition and prevent starvation-related deaths across sub-Saharan Africa, with Nigeria as a priority country. The partnership was announced on Monday when the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, led a delegation from the organisation and other agencies under the ministry to meet with the wife of the president, Oluremi Tinubu, to discuss areas of collaboration. According to a statement issued by Busola Kukoyi, the Senior Special Assistant on Media to Mrs Tinubu, the initiative aims to support Nigeria’s efforts to address hunger and child malnutrition through partnerships with the government. Operation End Starvation, an initiative of the Eleanor Crook Foundation, is a public-private partnership focused on ending child malnutrition and deaths associated with starvation across sub-Saharan Africa. The Chief Executive Officer of Operation End Starvation, Williams Moore, said the initiative aims to direct more than $1 billion towards preventing child deaths caused by starvation. He said the programme, supported by a grant from the US government and contributions from global philanthropists, would focus on sub-Saharan Africa over the next two years, with Nigeria among its priority countries. “We want to move one billion to end starvation in the next two years across Sub Saharan Africa. The burden is high but the capacity is also very high,” Mr Moore said. He said the US State Department had approved Nigeria’s inclusion in the initiative. “The foundation is impressed by Nigeria’s focus on combating acute malnutrition and we are seeking partnership for this global ‘Operation End Starvation’ programme,” he said. “We have met with the Nigeria health team and they are one of the best of many we have met.” Mr Pate said the partnership would support the government’s existing efforts to combat hunger and malnutrition. He cited the National Community Food Bank Programme, implemented in partnership with the Office of the First Lady, as one of the initiatives aimed at improving access to food across the country’s six geopolitical zones. “Nigeria is working hard to scale down its 6.4 million figure of acute child malnutrition, while also attending to the health of pregnant women and lactating mothers,” Mr Pate said. He added that several interventions were already underway to address the country’s nutritional challenges. Mrs Tinubu welcomed the proposed partnership, praising the expertise and commitment of government officials working across different sectors. “It’s been a delight working with Prof. Pate, Dr Muyi and others. I also work with the Ministry of Education and others. The manpower we have now in the ministries are so wonderful,” Mrs Tinubu said. She said President Bola Tinubu’s administration was working to overhaul the country’s systems, adding that Nigeria deserved better public services and effective use of available resources. “Nigeria deserves better and there is nothing we give to her that is too much because if the system works, it will ultimately come back to us,” she said. “I assure you that whatever aid you give us, this health team would put it to good use.” She also expressed confidence in the capacity of the country’s health team to ensure that assistance provided through the partnership was put to effective use. Nigeria continues to face significant challenges in addressing child malnutrition, particularly among children under five. According to figures cited by the health minister, the country has an estimated 6.4 million cases of acute child malnutrition. The federal government says it is working to reduce this burden while addressing the nutritional needs of pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers. Another data by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), estimates that about 100 children under five die of malnutrition per hour in Nigeria, approximately 2,400 children daily. It also explained that an estimated two million children under five in the country suffer from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), but only two out of every 10 children affected receive treatment. Research shows that malnutrition in Nigeria is a multifaceted issue with several contributing factors, which include poverty, food insecurity, inadequate infant and young child feeding practices, lack of access to healthcare, and poor sanitation. Factors like conflict, lack of education, and gender inequality also contribute. The 2023-2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey ( NDHS ) shows rising malnutrition across categories: stunting, wasting, and underweight children, with males slightly more affected than females. According to the data, 50.64 per cent of underweight children in Nigeria are male. The Eleanor Crook Foundation’s Operation End Starvation initiative aims to use direct partnerships with governments to demonstrate how large-scale investments can help end child malnutrition and prevent starvation-related deaths across sub-Saharan Africa
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/health/he.title_zh: 联邦政府与美国基金会合作，动员10亿美元应对儿童营养不良
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/health/he.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府正与美国机构“终结饥饿行动”合作，计划筹集超过10亿美元，对抗撒哈拉以南非洲的儿童营养不良问题，并防止与饥饿有关的死亡，尼日利亚被列为重点国家。该合作于星期一宣布。卫生与社会福利部协调部长穆罕默德·帕特率领该机构及卫生部其他机构代表团，会见总统夫人奥卢雷米·蒂努巴，讨论合作领域。根据蒂努巴夫人媒体高级特别助手布索拉·库科伊发表的声明，该倡议旨在通过与政府建立伙伴关系，支持尼日利亚解决饥饿和儿童营养不良问题的努力。“终结饥饿行动”是埃莉诺·克鲁克基金会发起的一项公私合作计划，宗旨是在撒哈拉以南非洲消除儿童营养不良以及与饥饿有关的死亡。“终结饥饿行动”首席执行官威廉斯·摩尔表示，该倡议计划投入超过10亿美元，防止饥饿造成的儿童死亡。他说，该项目得到美国政府拨款和全球慈善家出资的支持，未来两年将重点覆盖撒哈拉以南非洲，尼日利亚是重点国家之一。摩尔说：“我们希望在未来两年内投入10亿，在整个撒哈拉以南非洲终结饥饿。这里负担沉重，但应对能力也非常强。”他说，美国国务院已批准将尼日利亚纳入该倡议。他说：“基金会 impressed by Nigeria’s focus on combating acute malnutrition and we are seeking partnership for this global ‘Operation End Starvation’ programme. We have met with the Nigeria health team and they are one of the best of many we have met.” 帕特说，这项合作将支持政府现有的抗饥饿和营养不良工作。他提到与第一夫人办公室合作实施的“国家社区食品银行计划”，这是旨在改善全国六个地缘政治区域食品获取状况的项目之一。帕特说：“尼日利亚正努力降低急性儿童营养不良患者达640万人的数字，同时关注孕妇和哺乳期女性的健康。”他补充说，多项干预措施已在实施，以应对该国面临的营养挑战。蒂努巴夫人对拟议中的合作表示欢迎，并赞扬了在不同领域工作的政府官员的专业能力和投入精神。她说：“能与帕特教授、穆伊博士等人合作，我感到非常高兴。我也与教育部和其他机构合作。如今各部门拥有的人力都非常好。”她说，博拉·蒂努巴总统政府正在推动全面改革国家体系，并补充称，尼日利亚应享有更好的公共服务，也应更有效地利用现有资源。她说：“尼日利亚值得拥有更好的条件，我们给予她的一切都不算多，因为如果这个体系运转顺畅，最终也会回馈我们。我向你们保证，无论提供什么援助，这个卫生团队都会善加利用。”她还相信，该国卫生团队有能力确保通过这项合作提供的援助得到有效使用。尼日利亚在解决儿童营养不良问题方面仍面临重大挑战，尤其是五岁以下儿童。卫生部长援引的数据显示，该国估计有640万例急性儿童营养不良病例。联邦政府表示，正在努力减轻这一负担，同时满足孕妇和母乳喂养母亲的营养需求。联合国儿童基金会（UNICEF）的另一组数据估计，尼日利亚每小时约有100名五岁以下儿童死于营养不良，每天约有2,400名儿童死亡。该机构还解释说，该国估计有200万名五岁以下儿童患有重度急性营养不良（SAM），但每10名受影响儿童中只有2名接受治疗。研究显示，尼日利亚的营养不良是一个多因素问题，成因包括贫困、粮食不安全、婴幼儿喂养方式不当、无法获得医疗服务以及卫生条件恶劣。冲突、缺乏教育和性别不平等等因素也对此有所影响。《2023—2024年尼日利亚人口与健康调查》（NDHS）显示，各类营养不良问题均有所上升，包括发育迟缓、消瘦和体重不足，其中男童受影响程度略高于女童。数据显示，尼日利亚体重不足儿童中有50.64%为男性。埃莉诺·克鲁克基金会的“终结饥饿行动”倡议旨在通过与各国政府直接合作，展示大规模投资如何帮助撒哈拉以南非洲消除儿童营养不良并防止与饥饿有关的死亡

https://punchng.com/mercedes-benz-cuts-2.body: German premium carmaker Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday cut its outlook for the year, citing tough conditions in China and higher material costs. Core profit for 2026 is now expected to be on a par with the prior year’s 5.8 billion euros ($6.5 billion), the company said, down from a previously guided increase of at least 15 percent. Profit margins at the core car business are now seen at between two and three percent for the year, the firm said, down from the three to five percent previously expected. The news makes Mercedes the last of the big three German carmakers to lower their annual outlook after BMW and Volkswagen, both also citing weakness in China, the world’s largest car market. Mercedes-Benz’s vehicle deliveries in China — last year already at their lowest level since 2016 — fell a further 29 percent in the nine months to end-September. Local rivals such as Xiaomi and BYD have eaten into market share at the same time as a sluggish domestic economy has weighed on demand

https://leadership.ng/jpmorgans-nigerian.title: JPMorgan’s Nigerian Merchant Bank: 10 Things To Know
https://leadership.ng/jpmorgans-nigerian.summary: JPMorgan plans to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, with operations expected to begin before the end of 2026. JPMorgan deposited N50 billion ($38 million) with the Central Bank of Nigeria as it moves toward a merchant banking licence. The merchant bank would deepen an existing presence.
https://leadership.ng/jpmorgans-nigerian.summary_zh: 摩根大通计划在尼日利亚设立一家商人银行，预计将于2026年底前开始运营。摩根大通正向尼日利亚中央银行存入500亿奈拉（3,800万美元），以推进申请商人银行牌照。该商人银行将进一步深化其现有业务布局。
https://leadership.ng/jpmorgans-nigerian.body: 1. It plans to launch before the year ends . JPMorgan plans to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, with operations expected to begin before the end of 2026. 2. Regulatory approval is still pending . The plan was disclosed by the bank’s West Africa managing director and remains subject to regulatory approval. 3. It has put up the capital. JPMorgan deposited N50 billion ($38 million) with the Central Bank of Nigeria as it moves toward a merchant banking licence. 4. The approval timeline is less certain than the launch target . The central bank’s approval is expected by the end of 2026 or early 2027. The year-end launch target is therefore tight. 5. It is not a first arrival . Chase Manhattan, JPMorgan’s predecessor, opened a Lagos branch in 1961 and a representative office in 1982. The merchant bank would deepen an existing presence. 6. It already serves clients from Lagos . J.P. Morgan serves clients there through its Asset & Wealth Management and Commercial & Investment Bank businesses. 7. Ordinary customers should not expect branches or salary accounts . The merchant banking category focuses on corporate clients, investment banking and financial transactions. It is not a retail play. 8. Large companies stand to gain most . A licence would give JPMorgan a platform to serve companies seeking financing, manage cross-border transactions and support capital raising. Earlier reports linked the expansion to dollar loans for large companies, though that direction is not a confirmed product line. 9. Local banks will feel the competition. The entry could increase competition for corporate finance, investment banking and cross-border transactions. It could also push domestic institutions to improve services and open the door to partnerships. 10. A big name does not guarantee cheaper credit . An international banking name alone cannot guarantee cheaper borrowing, stable exchange rates or an investment surge. The real test is licence approval, launch, and whether it funds productive investment. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/jpmorgans-nigerian.body_zh: 1. 计划在年底前推出。JPMorgan计划在尼日利亚设立一家商人银行，预计将于2026年底前开始运营。2. 监管审批仍未完成。该计划由该银行西非区董事总经理披露，目前仍有待监管批准。3. 资本金已经到位。JPMorgan正向尼日利亚中央银行存入500亿奈拉（3,800万美元），以申请商人银行牌照。4. 审批时间表不如推出目标确定。预计尼日利亚中央银行将在2026年底或2027年初批准。因此，年内推出的目标较为紧张。5. 它并非首家进入当地市场。JPMorgan的前身大通曼哈顿银行于1961年在拉各斯设立分行，并于1982年设立代表处。这家商人银行将深化其在当地已有的布局。6. 它已经为拉各斯的客户提供服务。J.P. Morgan通过其资产与财富管理业务以及商业与投资银行业务为当地客户提供服务。7. 普通客户不应期待设有网点或薪资账户。商人银行类别主要面向企业客户，涵盖投资银行和金融交易，并非面向零售业务。8. 大型企业将从中受益最多。获得牌照将为JPMorgan提供一个平台，用于服务寻求融资、管理跨境交易以及支持资本募集的企业。此前有报道将此次扩张与面向大型企业的美元贷款联系起来，但这一方向尚未成为已经确认的产品线。9. 当地银行将感受到竞争。其进入市场可能加剧企业融资、投资银行和跨境交易领域的竞争，也可能推动本土机构改善服务并为合作伙伴关系打开大门。10. 大品牌并不保证融资成本更低。仅凭国际银行品牌，无法保证借贷成本降低、汇率稳定或投资激增。真正的考验是牌照能否获批、业务能否推出，以及能否为生产性投资提供资金。抢先掌握最新动态。获取实时报道、独家爆料和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，接收全天候更新 →

Unlock these with Subscription Ahead of Cuba’s resolution against the U.S. blockade to be taken up by the UN General Assembly on October 27, the Caribbean nation intensified its diplomatic outreach to the Global South on Sunday (October 25, 2026), with the Vice President of Cuba’s National Assembly of People’s Power and the Council of State Mari Machado meeting Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla here. Following the meeting with Ms. Machado, Mr. Birla said they had “discussed strengthening parliamentary exchanges, capacity-building and cooperation in healthcare and pharmaceuticals.” Cuba is participating in the BRICS Parliamentary Forum meeting as a partner country of the grouping. This comes two days after Cuba’s ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera accused the United States of carrying out a naval blockade that has created an acute energy crisis in his country. “Cuba is fully capable of defending itself. The U.S. is practising the Monroe Doctrine in our region,” Mr. Aguilera said, seeking support for Cuba’s UNGA resolution. Mr. Birla also met the Chairman of the State Duma of Russia, Vyacheslav Volodin, on Saturday (October 24), to discuss bilateral ties. India and Russia are marking the 80th anniversary of their bilateral relationship and the two dignitaries carried out a review of parliament-level exchanges between the two countries against the backdrop of unfolding global and regional developments. The Lok Sabha Speaker informed the Russian delegation about the steps taken to make parliamentary proceedings accessible in various Indian languages through Sansad Bhashini. According to a statement issued by the Parliament Secretariat, Mr. Birla highlighted the importance of using technology in making parliamentary functioning more accessible, efficient, and people-centric. 在联合国大会将于10月27日审议古巴针对美国封锁的决议之际，这个加勒比国家于周日（2026年10月25日）加大了对全球南方国家的外交联络力度。古巴全国人民权力代表大会副主席兼国务委员会成员玛丽·马查多在此会见了人民院议长奥姆·比尔拉。

与马查多女士会面后，比尔拉先生表示，双方“讨论了加强议会交流、能力建设以及在医疗保健和药品领域的合作”。古巴正以该集团伙伴国身份参加金砖国家议会论坛会议。

这是古巴驻印度大使胡安·卡洛斯·马桑·阿吉莱拉指责美国实施海上封锁两天后发生的事情；该封锁已给古巴造成严重的能源危机。阿吉莱拉先生说：“古巴完全有能力自卫。美国正在我们所在地区推行门罗主义。”他呼吁各方支持古巴在联合国大会提出的决议。

比尔拉先生还于周六（10月24日）会见了俄罗斯国家杜马主席维亚切斯拉夫·沃洛金，双方讨论了双边关系。印度和俄罗斯正纪念两国建立双边关系80周年；面对全球和地区局势的不断发展，两国政界人士回顾了两国之间的议会层级交流。

人民院议长向俄罗斯代表团介绍了通过 Sansad Bhashini 让议会 proceedings 以多种印度语言进行的相关举措。根据议会秘书处发表的声明，比尔拉先生强调，应利用技术让议会运作更加便于公众参与、更加高效，并以人民为中心。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.summary: Promoters of Coin Finance Company Limited have demanded the return of N100.35 million paid to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to operate as a finance house, following the suspension of new licence applications. According to him, the investors paid N100 million as capital deposit, N100,000 as application fee and N250,000 as licensing fee on July 16, 2025, bringing the total payment to N100.35 million.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.summary_zh: Coin Finance Company Limited 的推广者要求退回向尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）缴纳的1.0035亿奈拉，以继续作为金融公司运营。此前，在暂停受理新牌照申请后，相关人士表示，投资者于2025年7月16日缴纳了1亿奈拉资本保证金、10万奈拉申请费和25万奈拉牌照费，总付款额达到1.0035亿奈拉。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.body: Promoters of Coin Finance Company Limited have demanded the return of N100.35 million paid to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to operate as a finance house, following the suspension of new licence applications. A representative of the promoters, Mr Christopher Itua, made the demand in a statement, saying the funds had remained with the apex bank for about 15 months without the proposed institution progressing. According to him, the investors paid N100 million as capital deposit, N100,000 as application fee and N250,000 as licensing fee on July 16, 2025, bringing the total payment to N100.35 million. The payment was made as part of the requirements for licensing Coin Finance Company Ltd as a finance house. Itua said CBN officials informed the promoters in October 2025 that processing of new finance house applications had been suspended until further notice. He explained that following the suspension, he wrote the CBN Department of Financial Policy and Regulation on October 15, 2025, requesting the return of the funds with applicable interest. The promoters later petitioned the CBN Consumer Protection Department on May 18, 2026, and sent a follow-up letter on July 7, but said they had received neither a refund timeline nor a substantive update. “It has now been over 14 months since the CBN took possession of our capital,” Itua said in his latest appeal to the CBN Governor. He said the proposed finance house was designed to address a financing gap at the grassroots and strengthen economic activity at the micro level. “The finance house is meant to boost grassroots empowerment, a sector that is very important to strengthening the micro economy,” he said. Itua noted inadequate institutions serving small businesses and grassroots entrepreneurs remained a major constraint despite improvements in the broader macroeconomic environment. “The macro is doing well, but the micro is not. This is the missing link because there are not enough institutions to power that sector,” he said. According to him, the prolonged retention of the capital had stalled the promoters’ plans to establish the institution and provide financial support at the grassroots. The investors are asking the CBN to calculate applicable interest on the N100.35 million from July 16, 2025, when the funds were deposited, until the date of release. “The prolonged silence and structural failure to return capital deposits directly undermines the Federal Government’s ease-of-doing-business initiatives,” Itua said. The promoters said their payment receipts, transaction documents and previous correspondence had been submitted to support the request. Itua appealed to the CBN Governor to intervene and resolve the matter administratively, stressing that the promoters had repeatedly used the bank’s established channels. They said continued inaction could compel them to pursue further administrative and legal channels, although they preferred to resolve the matter without escalation. The promoters are seeking the immediate return of the N100.35 million, together with applicable interest from July 16, 2025, until the funds are released. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.title_zh: 暂停发放许可证：投资者要求尼日利亚中央银行退还1.0035亿奈拉
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.body_zh: Coin Finance Company Limited的发起人要求尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）退还1.0035亿奈拉，以作为获准运营金融机构的资金，原因是新的牌照申请已被暂停。发起人代表克里斯托弗·伊图阿先生在一份声明中提出这一要求，称拟议机构尚未取得进展，但资金已在这家最高银行滞留约15个月。据他介绍，投资者于2025年7月16日支付1亿奈拉作为资本金、10万奈拉作为申请费以及25万奈拉作为牌照费，总付款额达到1.0035亿奈拉。这笔付款是为Coin Finance Company Ltd取得金融公司牌照而支付的费用。伊图阿表示，CBN官员于2025年10月告知发起人，新的金融公司申请处理工作已暂停，直至另行通知。他解释道，暂停后，他于2025年10月15日致函CBN金融政策与监管部，要求退还资金并支付适用利息。发起人后来于2026年5月18日向CBN消费者保护部提交申诉，并于7月7日发送了后续信函，但称既未收到退款时间表，也未收到实质性进展更新。伊图阿在最新一次向CBN行长提出的申诉中表示：“如今，CBN接管我们的资本金已经超过14个月。”他说，拟议中的金融公司旨在弥合基层融资缺口，并加强微型层面的经济活动。他说：“这家公司旨在推动基层赋权，而基层赋权对强化微型经济非常重要。”伊图阿指出，尽管整体宏观经济环境有所改善，但服务小型企业和基层创业者的机构仍不充足，这仍是主要制约因素。他说：“宏观层面表现良好，但微观层面并非如此。这是缺失的环节，因为没有足够的机构为该领域提供动力。”据他称，长期滞留资本金已经阻碍发起人设立该机构并在基层提供金融支持。投资者要求CBN从2025年7月16日资金存入之日起，至实际发放之日止，按照1.0035亿奈拉计算适用利息。伊图阿说：“长期沉默以及未能退还资本金的结构性失职，直接削弱了联邦政府改善营商环境的努力。”发起人表示，他们已经提交付款收据、交易文件及以往往来函件，以支持退款请求。伊图阿呼吁CBN行长介入，通过行政途径解决此事，强调发起人此前已多次使用该行既定渠道处理问题。他们表示，若继续不作为，可能迫使他们采取进一步的行政和法律途径，尽管他们更希望在事态升级前解决此事。发起人要求立即退还1.0035亿奈拉，并支付从2025年7月16日起至资金发放之日止的适用利息。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都领地以及世界各地设有办公室。该报是尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，覆盖所有平台，为政界、商业界、专业人士和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层服务，同时充当有抱负者、千禧一代探索新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会的交叉领域。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki, has said that the people of his constituency cannot longer sleep with their two eyes closed due to the frequent abduction of the people in the constituency. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/we-n.summary_zh: Nasarawa州议会 Lafia Central选区议员 Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki表示，由于该选区频繁发生人员绑架事件，当地居民已无法安然闭眼入睡。这位议员周二在议会上以公共利益事项为由提出这一问题，敦促安全机构和州政府采取更有力的行动，保护公民的生命和财产安全。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/we-n.body: Member representing the Lafia Central constituency at the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki, has said that the people of his constituency cannot longer sleep with their two eyes closed due to the frequent abduction of the people in the constituency. The lawmaker, while raising the issue on the floor of the House on Tuesday as a matter of public interest, urged the security agencies and the state government to be more committed to protecting the lives and property of its citizens. He said, “Mr Speaker and my honourable colleagues, I rise on a matter of frequent kidnapping in my constituency. “Yesterday, in Agyaragu Lafia, two people were kidnapped. Days back, in Agunji Lafia, people were kidnapped. “As I am talking, the two people kidnapped yesterday are in the hands of the kidnappers, and they are demanding ransom. “Security agencies and the state government should rise up to curtail the rate of kidnapping and other forms of insecurity in my constituency,” he appealed. Reacting to the alarm over a fresh resurgence of kidnapping incidents across the State, the Speaker of the House, Dr Danladi Jatau, said that the State capital and some parts of the State are experiencing frequent abductions that have caused fear and economic setbacks to the State. The speaker appreciated the mover of the motion and other colleagues for their positive contributions on the issue. “The resolution of the House is to the effect that we urge His Excellency, Gov. Abdullahi Sule, to direct all security agencies, the Commissioner of Police, and the DSS and NSCDC to beam their satellites across the state to curtail the rate of kidnapping. “All hands must be on deck, especially Chiefs and Village Heads, in collaboration with Vigilantes to identify strange people in their communities,” he said. The Speaker directed the Clerk of the House to communicate the House resolution to Gov. Sule for his necessary action. Also contributing, Hon. Esson Mairiga Esq, Hon. Onarigu Onah Kana, Hon. Ibrahim Abdullahi Sa’ad, Hon. Suleiman Yakubu Azara, Rt Hon. Abel Yakubu Bala and Hon. Larry Ven-Bawa supported the motion and called on the state government to beef up security across the state in order to curtail the rate of kidnapping in the state. They lamented how kidnapping is affecting the lives of their people negatively. The lawmakers, however, appreciated the efforts of Gov. Sule in terms of security but urged him and security agencies to be more committed to tackling the rate of kidnapping across the state. The lawmakers collectively called on security agencies to intensify operations. They called on both the federal and state governments to purchase sophisticated weapons via technology to tackle insecurity in the state. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/we-n.title_zh: “我们再也无法闭着双眼安然入睡”——纳萨拉瓦州议员痛斥绑架事件
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/we-n.body_zh: 纳萨拉瓦州议会拉菲亚中部选区议员、尊敬的所罗门·雅库布·阿克瓦希基表示，由于该选区频繁发生人员绑架事件，当地民众已无法安然入睡。这名议员周二在议会发言，将此事作为涉及公众利益的问题提出，敦促安全机构和州政府更加坚决地保护公民的生命和财产安全。他说：“议长先生及各位尊敬的同僚，我今天要提出我所选区频繁发生绑架的问题。“昨天，在阿格亚拉圭拉菲亚，有两人遭到绑架。几天前，在阿贡吉拉菲亚，也有人遭到绑架。“就在我讲话时，昨天被绑架的两人仍控制在绑匪手中，绑匪正在索要赎金。“安全机构和州政府应当采取行动，遏止我所选区的绑架及其他形式的不安全事件。”他呼吁道。针对全州绑架事件再次激增引发的警报，议长丹拉迪·贾陶博士表示，州首府及州内部分地区频繁发生绑架，给当地造成恐惧并带来经济倒退。议长对动议发起人及其他同僚就此问题作出的积极贡献表示感谢。他说：“议会的决议是，敦请尊敬的州长阿卜杜拉希·苏莱指示所有安全机构、警察局长以及国家情报局和国家民防委员会调动卫星监测力量覆盖全州，以遏止绑架事件的发生。“所有人都必须积极参与，尤其是各位酋长和村长，要与治安志愿人员合作，找出社区中的可疑人员。”他说。议长指示议会书记将议会决议传达给苏莱州长，以便其采取必要行动。尊敬的埃松·迈里加律师、尊敬的奥纳里古·奥纳·卡纳、尊敬的易卜拉欣·阿卜杜拉希·萨阿德、尊敬的苏莱曼·雅库布·阿扎拉、尊敬的阿贝尔·雅库布·巴拉阁下及尊敬的拉里·文-巴瓦也支持该动议，并呼吁州政府加强全州安全措施，以遏止该州绑架事件的发生。他们对绑架事件给当地民众生活造成的负面影响表示痛心。不过，这些议员对苏莱州长在安全方面采取的措施表示赞赏，同时敦促他与安全机构更加坚决地打击全州范围内的绑架问题。议员们一致呼吁安全机构加强行动，并呼吁联邦政府和州政府通过技术手段采购先进武器，以应对该州的不安全局势。本文所述评论不代表《Vanguard》报或该报任何员工的观点

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/tinu.summary_zh: 众议院副议长本杰明·卡卢表示，总统博拉·蒂努布已批准为东南部农村家庭提供50万套太阳能灯。卡卢在“新希望点亮”倡议启动仪式上披露了这一消息。活动中，向阿比亚州本德联邦选区的各社区分发了26台变压器以及1万套太阳能灯和风扇。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/tinu.body: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has said President Bola Tinubu has approved the provision of 500,000 solar-powered lights for rural households in the South-East. Kalu disclosed this at the flag-off of the Renewed Hope Light-Up initiative, during which 26 transformers and 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans were distributed to communities in Bende Federal Constituency, Abia State. He said 42,000 households in the constituency had been earmarked to benefit from the initiative, with the first batch of 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans expected to be delivered within two weeks. According to him, 1,000 units had already been distributed as a pilot scheme, with representatives from the federal constituency’s wards confirming their functionality. Kalu said the initiative was designed to make the benefits of the Renewed Hope Agenda tangible to rural residents, particularly households that had struggled with unreliable electricity supply. He described the planned provision of solar-powered lights to 42,000 households in a single federal constituency as unprecedented, adding that the initiative would help improve access to electricity in underserved communities. The lawmaker representing Bende South Constituency in the Abia State House of Assembly, Emmanuel Ndubuisi, described the intervention as significant, noting that some communities had been without electricity for about two years following transformer failures. A representative of the project contractor, Solar Systems Nigeria, Peter Oko, said the initiative would also provide opportunities for youth training and empowerment. He assured beneficiaries of the company’s commitment to delivering quality and reliable services. Earlier, Director-General of the Ben Kalu Campaign Council, Emma Trump Eke, described the intervention as a landmark project for Bende Federal Constituency.
